findings.claim: ADR-0008 item #3 says v2 replaces v1's 'modify to an echo' with 'a real deny with a reason (each agent's native field, ADR-0001 adapter table)' for the whole adapter set, to fix #1134 (Codex auto-review flagged the echo as instruction drift). The copilot-cli formatter still implements the old v1 pattern: routing.mjs's bash-command-redirect decision (lines 769/800/813, shape {action:'modify', updatedInput:{command:'echo "..."'}}) reaches formatters.mjs's copilot-cli.modify branch, which returns {modifiedArgs: updatedInput} unconditionally — it is never converted to deny. claude-code and codex each have an explicit special case in formatters.mjs that turns this same shape into a hard permissionDecision:'deny' (claude-code: isBashCommandRedirect check at line ~33; codex: 'FAIL CLOSED' comment near line ~155); copilot-cli has no such special case.
findings.evidence: hooks/core/formatters.mjs:123-125 copilot-cli.modify: '(updatedInput) => ({ modifiedArgs: updatedInput })' — no isBashCommandRedirect branch, no deny fallback, unlike the claude-code block (lines 29-57) and the codex block (comment: '#845: modern Codex ... honors permissionDecision:"allow" + updatedInput ... otherwise FAIL CLOSED'). ADR-0008 table row 3: '`modify` to an `echo` command -> A real deny with a reason ... Fixes #1134'.
findings.fix: Add the same isBashCommandRedirect special case to the copilot-cli formatter block: when updatedInput carries a `command` key, emit permissionDecision:'deny' with permissionDecisionReason extracted from the echo payload (same logic already factored out for claude-code), instead of passing modifiedArgs through. Verify against the live `@github/copilot` binary (the README already cites 1.0.60 for hook event names) whether modifiedArgs.command is honored at all before deciding; if it is silently ignored (same class of bug the codex #845 fix addresses), this is the live #1134-equivalent for Copilot CLI and must be fail-closed, not pass-through.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY 9f34c6f1 2026-06-21 'Add GitHub Copilot CLI + Antigravity CLI (agy) support' (#787) — the commit message describes a 'json-stdio hook adapter with six events' and documents the fail-open dispatcher behavior, but never documents or tests command-rewrite (modifiedArgs) semantics for Copilot CLI, unlike the codex #845 fix which has an explicit runtime version probe (`codexSupportsRewrite`) and the claude-code block which has an explicit '/diagnose Phase 4 forced-deny probe' comment. ORIGINAL_INTENT (commit body): ship MCP + hook parity fast for two new CLIs on top of 'next's existing adapter registration', not to design new rewrite semantics. REGRESSION_RISK: if the host does not honor modifiedArgs for a PreToolUse veto (plausible, since no verification comment exists, mirroring the exact gap that caused #845 for Codex and the drift flagged in #1134 for Codex's echo pattern), then curl/wget/inline-HTTP commands run unmodified on Copilot CLI even though ADR-0008 declares this scope 'deny' for every agent, directly breaking the hard-deny decision and ADR-0016 (large output must not enter context) for this one host. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: the fix must fail closed (hard deny), not fail open, and must not rely on an unverified host capability; do not restore the v1 echo-as-pseudo-deny shape anywhere, since that is the exact pattern ADR-0008 #3 was written to remove.

findings.claim: The round1 review of the agent's source directory (3813 bytes, smallest of the comparable agent-* reviews next to agent-pi 4741, agent-kiro 5690, agent-zcode 6160, agent-vs-code-copilot 6425) sampled only the project-source fallback chain (ADR-0007/Q11) and the E2E credential conflict (TECH-SPEC §365). It did not read hooks/core/formatters.mjs's copilot-cli branch or routing.mjs's modify call sites at all, so it never checked the enforcement/deny mechanism against ADR-0008 item #3 — the single decision this review round was asked to focus on ('hooks ... deny/rewrite/replace'). That is a real gap in round1's coverage, not just a smaller file by chance: the missed file (formatters.mjs) is shared across every adapter and is where the actual ADR-0008-vs-code contradiction above lives.
